items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: And then there’s this terrific pianist, a friend of mine I haven’t seen in years who lives out in Jersey and he just teaches and plays in bars.

ctx.x: Well he was like this inside, and everybody, Stan Kenton was after him and I think he might have been with him for a minute and he quit. He just didn’t want to deal with all that. He wound up working in a post office and talking about aliens. And then there’s this terrific pianist, a friend of mine I haven’t seen in years who lives out in Jersey and he just teaches and plays in bars. His name is Bill Trillia. He plays on a Mingus record. There’s guys like that. And then there was this folk hero Tony Frasella, a…
